Screening is performed before incorporation and refreshed annually; findings are documented in the AML file and reported to TRACFIN in accordance with Article L561-5.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: INPI / Guichet des Entreprises — official online business formalities portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The official administrative language is French; the corporate name must be expressed in Latin script. A name originating in a foreign script must be transliterated into Latin characters and may be accompanied by a French trade name. The name must not conflict with pre-existing registered names or trademarks and must not contain prohibited words.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The initial reservation is valid for 30 days and is not renewable; the applicant may refile a new request after the period. Upon rejection, the applicant may lodge an administrative appeal with the INPI section of the competent commercial registry and simultaneously request judicial review before the Tribunal judiciaire in Paris within two months of notification, supported by a legal memorandum and corrected name documentation.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or business-center domiciliation is permissible for the registered office and administrative operations under Article L123-10 of the French Commercial Code. For a toy-manufacturing corporate vehicle without a local factory, a commercial office address in France is sufficient for RCS registration; however, the statutory license for toy manufacturing and DGCCRF product-safety responsibilities may require a physical operating location if the entity declares local production or warehousing.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk of 5% per year for an unannounced physical on-site inspection by DGCCRF for companies in the toy trade, rising to approximately 15% during national toy-safety enforcement operations (e.g., 'Opération Jouets de Noël').

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Code de commerce (French Commercial Code), Book II: Articles L.227-1 through L.227-20 (Société par Actions Simplifiée); L.224-1 (registered office and presidency); Décret n° 2023-857 (digital Guichet Unique filing); Loi Pacte n° 2019-486; Toy Safety Directive 2009/48/EC transposed by Décret n° 2010-1661.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce compétent (Registry of the Commercial Court of the registered-office department), filed digitally through the INPI Guichet Unique at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Dossier M0 — Demande d'immatriculation d'une société (SAS), submitted with certified copies of the Statuts and all statutory annexes.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital for a French SAS; the capital is freely fixed in the Statuts. Cash contributions must be fully paid up upon subscription and deposited into a blocked escrow account with a French bank or the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations (CDC) until the Kbis is issued. In-kind contributions exceeding €30,000 or representing more than half of the capital require a Commissaire aux Apports valuation report.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION — [SAS NAME]. Held on [date] at the registered office, the founders and President unanimously resolve: 1. Ratification of incorporation of the Société par Actions Simplifiée engaging in eco-friendly beechwood turning and sale of Montessori wooden toddler toys. 2. Adoption of registered office at [Address], France. 3. Confirmation of full subscription and payment of share capital of €[Amount], allocated per the Articles. 4. Appointment of [Name] as President, [Name] as Directeur Général, and [Name] as Commissaire aux Comptes where applicable. 5. Authorization of the President to file the M0 form, obtain the Kbis and complete publication formalities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft, sign and notarise the Articles of Association (Statuts) of the SAS
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Founding shareholders acting under private signature, or before a French notaire (notarial deed) where contributions in kind or real property are involved.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Statuts in accordance with Articles L.227-1 to L.227-20 of the French Commercial Code, including the corporate name, duration (99 years), registered office, corporate object (eco-friendly beechwood turning and manufacture of non-toxic sensory Montessori wooden blocks), share capital and classes, share-transfer approval (agrément) rules, presidency and management powers, and dispute-resolution provisions. Each founder must initial and sign all pages; the President countersigns. If contributions in kind are made, instruct the Commissaire aux Apports to prepare the valuation report to be annexed to the Statuts.
required_dossiers: Draft Statuts of the SAS in French
Valid passport or national identity card of each founding shareholder
Attestation de non-condamnation (declaration of no criminal conviction) for the first President
Kbis or foreign registry extract for any corporate shareholder
Valuation report of in-kind contributions, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a clause is queried by the notary or by a founder, sign an avenant (amendment) restating the clause and annex it to the final signed Statuts before filing; no registry elapsed-time is incurred.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open the temporary escrow account and deposit the paid-up share capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Any licensed French commercial bank, or the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations (CDC) in Paris as fallback depositary.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary non-interest-bearing bank account in the name of the company in formation. Credit the account with 100% of the subscribed cash capital. Obtain the bank's Attestation de dépôt de fonds (blocked-funds certificate), which must identify the future SAS, the amount deposited, and the irrevocable nature of the funds. Funds remain blocked until the bank receives a certified copy of the Kbis after registration.
required_dossiers: Temporary account opening application for the future SAS
Final signed version of the Statuts
Identity documents of all cash-contributing shareholders
Source-of-funds declaration and bank reference letter for contributions above €10,000
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses on anti-money-laundering grounds, provide strengthened due-diligence documentation (source of wealth, bank statements); if all commercial banks decline, deposit the capital with the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations, which is statutorily obliged to receive it.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publish the statutory formation notice (annonce légale) in an authorised legal-announcement journal
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A Journal d'Annonces Légales formally authorised by the préfecture of the département where the registered office is located.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Transmit the insertion text to the legal-announcement journal. The notice must state the corporate form (SAS), corporate name, share capital, registered-office address, corporate object, duration and the commercial registry where the company will be registered. The journal editor verifies the content and issues the Certificat de parution after publication. This certificate is a mandatory annex to the registration dossier.
required_dossiers: Signed draft of the legal announcement text
Attestation of corporate-name availability and non-opposition from the registry
Copy of the Statuts' purpose clause for editorial verification
Payment receipt of the statutory publication fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry rejects the announcement as non-conforming, publish a corrective insert (insertion rectificative) in the same journal and annex the corrective certificate to the filing dossier.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submit the complete digital incorporation dossier to the INPI Guichet Unique
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet Unique national online portal (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr), which routes the file to the competent Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to the portal, select 'création d'entreprise', form 'SAS', and complete the M0 declaration fields: corporate name, capital, registered office, corporate object, duration, President, statutory auditors if appointed, and commencement of operations. Upload the certified PDF copy of the Statuts and all statutory annexes. Verify identity via FranceConnect or electronic signature. Pay online the state filing fee (droit fixe) and registry fees. Retain the dossier reference number (ID4) for tracking.
required_dossiers: Completed M0 digital declaration
Signed Statuts in PDF
Attestation de dépôt de fonds from the bank or CDC
Certificat de parution of the legal announcement
Proof of registered-office availability (bail, acte de jouissance or deed of ownership)
Identity documents and attendation de non-condamnation of the President
Identity documents of all shareholders
Commissaire aux Apports report, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the dossier is pending or rejected, the INPI sends a notice of missing or illegible items; cure by uploading supplementary documents within 15 calendar days via the same portal. Continued non-cure results in formal rejection, which may be contested before the Greffe or the Président du Tribunal de Commerce.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registry examination, issuance of the Kbis and release of escrowed capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce du ressort du siège social (Registry of the Commercial Court within whose jurisdiction the registered office is established).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The registry checks the legal regularity of the Statuts, capital deposit certificate, legal-announcement certificate, and director declarations. Upon approval, the company is entered into the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) and receives the extrait Kbis, SIREN/SIRET identifiers, and French intra-EU VAT number. Present the Kbis to the bank or CDC to release the escrowed capital and open the final operating bank account. Integrate the Kbis, SIREN and VAT number into Amazon Seller Central, Stripe and commercial contracts.
required_dossiers: INPI dossier reference number and e-proof of filing
Payment receipts for state and registry fees
Any supplementary documents requested by the Greffe (revisions, translations, apostilles)
Kbis application confirmation generated by the Guichet Unique
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Greffe raises a substantive observation, rectify and resubmit the affected document within 15 calendar days of notification. Failure to cure leads to rejection, which is appealable to the Président du Tribunal de Commerce within 15 days of the rejection notice.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Préfecture du département (ICPE environmental permitting), DREETS — Direction régionale de l'économie, de l'emploi, du travail et des solidarités (labour, machinery and occupational safety), and DGCCRF — Direction générale de la concurrence, de la consommation et de la répression des fraudes (toy safety and consumer product market surveillance).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Récépissé de déclaration ICPE Rubrique 2921-B (wood transformation workshop) and CE certificate of conformity for the wooden toys under Toy Safety Directive 2009/48/EC (harmonised standards EN 71-1, EN 71-2, EN 71-3 and, where applicable, EN 62115).

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: DREAL — Direction régionale de l'environnement, de l'aménagement et du logement of the Ministère de la Transition écologique.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration (Déclaration) under ICPE Rubrique 2921-B where the aggregate installed mechanical power of woodworking machinery exceeds 20 kW; below 20 kW the workshop is exempt from formal ICPE filing but remains subject to wood-dust and waste-handling duties. A full environmental impact assessment (étude d'impact) is not triggered for a small wood-turning site located outside Natura 2000 zones, sensitive water catchments, or areas subject to specific protection orders.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wood dust occupational exposure: 1.1 mg/m³ total inhalable dust for softwood and 0.2 mg/m³ for beech and oak (class 1A carcinogenic wood dust) per Code du travail Article R.4222-10 and the applicable ministerial fixation order; VOC content of water-based coatings limited to 100 g/L per Directive 2004/42/EC Phase II; wastewater discharge to municipal sewer: pH 6.5-8.5, suspended solids below 300 mg/L, COD below 600 mg/L with a prior déversement declaration; waste wood offcuts consigned to a registered waste carrier with bordereau de suivi des déchets.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety: if the premises include a public showroom, obtain the CCDSA commission de sécurité visit and ERP exploitation authorization (5th category); for a purely industrial workshop, maintain a Fire Safety Register, install spark detection and extraction-silo protection, and file the fire-safety declaration with the local SIS (service départemental d'incendie et de secours). Structural clearance: the lease or property deed must evidence structural load capacity for the installed machinery, confirmed by an attestation de solidité structurelle. Occupational clearance: complete and sign the DUERP (Document Unique d'Évaluation des Risques Professionnels), register the employer with CARSAT, certify machine guards per Décret n° 92-767, and arrange periodic verification of wood-dust extraction systems by an accredited inspection body.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) via official portal impots.gouv.fr
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: French SAS obtain SIREN/SIRET through guichet-entreprises.fr; foreign entities register for TVA FR identification by submitting incorporation documents, proof of address, and tax forms directly to DGFiP
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Entity-level taxation under Impôt sur les Sociétés (IS); no check-the-box elections available; hybrid mismatch rules permitted under EU ATAD directive

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory facturation électronique with real-time reporting to DGFiP via PEP interface; API integration required for digital stamping and clearance

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% VAT rate for goods exported outside EU or intra-EU supplies with proof of dispatch; offshore services to non-EU customers
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Fines up to 80% of evaded VAT plus interest; retrospective clawback of zero-rating benefits if export not substantiated

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France, with prudential and payment-services supervision by the Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution and monetary-policy oversight within the European System of Central Banks led by the European Central Bank. Foreign-exchange activity is principally governed by European Union free-movement-of-capital rules, French anti-money-laundering legislation, sanctions law, customs rules, and payment-services regulations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible for current-account and capital-account transactions. A French SAS may receive, hold, convert, and remit euros and foreign currencies without a general foreign-exchange licence, mandatory central-bank approval, capital repatriation restriction, or foreign-currency retention limit. Current-account payments, import settlements, export receipts, service fees, royalties, interest, dividends, and intercompany balances are generally transferable through regulated payment institutions or credit institutions, subject to bank AML, sanctions, tax, and source-of-funds controls. Capital movements, shareholder loans, capital contributions, acquisitions, and disposals are also generally unrestricted, subject to EU and French foreign-investment screening where a transaction concerns a protected strategic sector, sanctions, anti-money-laundering controls, or statistical reporting. Dividend and liquidation distributions require distributable profits or legally available reserves, valid corporate approvals, accounts supporting the distribution, and compliance with French withholding-tax rules. The ordinary French domestic dividend withholding rate is generally 25%, subject to applicable treaty relief, the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive exemption, beneficial-ownership requirements, anti-abuse rules, and documentary procedures. Payments to related parties must also satisfy transfer-pricing, deductibility, interest-limitation, and beneficial-owner requirements.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France has no general statutory export-proceeds surrender obligation, mandatory conversion ratio, or fixed deadline requiring a French SAS to convert foreign-currency export receipts into euros. Export proceeds may generally remain in foreign-currency accounts or be converted at the company's treasury discretion. Export transactions must be properly documented through commercial invoices, transport records, customs export declarations, customer contracts, and banking references. Banks may request evidence of the underlying trade, payer identity, ultimate beneficial owner, sanctions screening, and economic purpose before crediting or releasing funds. Statistical reporting may apply to cross-border transactions under Banque de France or European statistical-survey requirements, generally through bank reporting or direct declarations when thresholds and reporting notices apply. Cash or certain negotiable monetary instruments physically entering or leaving the European Union at or above EUR 10,000 must be declared to customs. No export-receipt conversion ratio or statutory repatriation timetable applies to ordinary merchandise exports.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium to High for operational payments, collections, cards, and selected foreign-currency flows, but not a complete substitute for a French relationship bank. An electronic-money institution or payment institution licensed in France or another European Economic Area state may provide services in France through passporting, an establishment, or an authorised agent, subject to applicable notification and AML requirements. Offshore providers without an EU licence, passport, French establishment, or authorised agent should not be used for regulated payment services to French customers. EMI balances are safeguarded customer funds and are not bank deposits; deposit-guarantee protection generally does not apply. Providers may restrict regulated goods, marketplace flows, high-volume cross-border receipts, third-party funds, cash activity, sanctioned jurisdictions, and rapid settlement patterns. A fintech account should be paired with a French or EU credit-institution account for capital escrow, tax payments, reserve liquidity, and business continuity.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French law does not impose a universal requirement for all SAS directors or shareholders to appear physically at a bank branch. Remote onboarding, certified digital identification, video identification, qualified electronic signatures, and notarised or apostilled corporate documents may be accepted at the institution's discretion. Banks may nevertheless require a physical meeting or enhanced video interview for non-resident directors, foreign ultimate beneficial owners, complex ownership chains, newly incorporated entities, higher-risk jurisdictions, unusual business models, or unexplained international flows. The company should expect to provide the registered-office evidence, Kbis or incorporation extract, statutes, beneficial-owner declaration, tax identification details, board or shareholder resolutions, director and UBO identification, proof of address, business plan, expected transaction profile, supplier and customer evidence, source-of-funds evidence, and evidence supporting the share-capital deposit.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shareholder, director, or ultimate beneficial owner with incomplete identity, address, tax-residence, or ownership information
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified passport or national identity document; recent proof of residential address; tax-residence declaration and identification number; notarised ownership chart; beneficial-owner declaration; corporate registry extracts for every intermediate entity; director appointment evidence; sanctions and politically exposed person screening record; signed explanation of ownership purpose.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque, layered, nominee, trust, bearer-share, or offshore ownership structure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete chain-of-ownership chart to natural persons; constitutional documents; registers of shareholders and directors; trust deed and trustee or protector information where relevant; UBO attestations; independent registry extracts; source-of-wealth narrative; legal opinions or certified translations where requested; written confirmation that no undisclosed nominee arrangement exists.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Newly incorporated SAS with no operating history, limited financial statements, or no demonstrated commercial substance
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed business plan; three-year cash-flow forecast; product catalogue; manufacturing and distribution contracts; purchase orders; customer pipeline; supplier quotations; warehouse or fulfilment arrangements; website and marketplace evidence; staffing plan; funding schedule; explanation of expected monthly transaction volumes and countries.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Toy manufacturing or distribution activity involving product-safety, import, customs, or regulatory exposure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Product descriptions and HS classifications; supplier due-diligence files; CE-marking and EU toy-safety compliance records; technical documentation; EN 71 test reports where applicable; conformity assessment materials; import and customs documents; insurance certificates; recall and product-liability procedures; evidence that payment flows match genuine goods transactions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected payments involving high-risk jurisdictions, sanctioned territories, restricted counterparties, or unusual intermediary banks
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Country-risk matrix; counterparty registry extracts; beneficial-owner information; sanctions-screening results; end-use and end-user certificates; contracts, invoices, bills of lading, and customs records; written sanctions policy; escalation and rejection procedures; documented commercial rationale for each jurisdiction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large shareholder funding, intercompany loans, rapid capital movements, or funds inconsistent with declared turnover
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed capital-increase or loan agreement; shareholder and board approvals; bank statements; audited or certified financial statements; lender source-of-funds and source-of-wealth evidence; tax treatment memorandum; repayment schedule; transfer-pricing support; funds-flow diagram; reconciliation of inbound funds to accounting records.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume marketplace, card, refund, chargeback, or third-party collection activity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Marketplace agreements; acquiring contracts; payment-flow map; customer and merchant role analysis; refund and chargeback policy; transaction-monitoring controls; segregation of customer funds where applicable; reconciliation procedures; expected gross and net settlement profile; fraud-prevention and customer-verification controls.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of personal accounts, cash-intensive settlement, virtual assets, or unexplained transfers between related parties
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Formal prohibition on personal-account use; treasury policy; approved bank-account register; accounting reconciliations; explanation and remediation of historical transactions; source-of-funds evidence; related-party register; board approvals; independent accountant confirmation; documented virtual-asset prohibition unless separately approved and regulated.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Deposit SAS share capital into a designated capital escrow account at a French bank or eligible notary before incorporation or capital increase. Use a transfer narrative identifying the subscriber, SAS name, capital contribution, and incorporation or capital-increase reference. After receipt of the deposit certificate and registration, release the funds into the operational account. For post-incorporation equity, route funds against executed shareholder or board resolutions, amended statutes where required, subscription forms, and the relevant corporate filing. For shareholder loans, use a signed loan agreement, arm's-length terms, maturity, interest, repayment mechanics, transfer-pricing support, and any applicable French tax or statistical reporting. Use SEPA Credit Transfer for euro payments within the SEPA area and SWIFT cross-border transfer for other currencies or jurisdictions. France does not operate a universal foreign-exchange purpose-code regime; the bank's payment-purpose field, invoice or contract reference, and accounting classification should accurately state capital contribution, shareholder loan, intercompany funding, or operating receipt. Banks may verify source of funds, source of wealth, UBO identity, sanctions status, corporate authority, beneficial ownership, and consistency with the declared business model before crediting or releasing funds.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SEPA Credit Transfer or SEPA Instant Credit Transfer for eligible euro suppliers and SWIFT customer credit transfer for non-SEPA or foreign-currency payments. A SWIFT MT103 is the legacy customer-payment format; banks are migrating to ISO 20022 payment messages, principally pacs.008, so payment instructions should follow the executing bank's current format. For higher-value or higher-risk imports, use documentary commercial letters of credit, standby letters of credit, documentary collections, open-account settlement with trade-credit insurance, or supply-chain-finance programmes. A commercial LC should identify the applicant, beneficiary, issuing and advising banks, amount, currency, expiry, shipment terms, Incoterms, presentation period, required transport and customs documents, insurance requirements, and UCP 600 or other agreed rules. Maintain purchase orders, invoices, transport documents, customs entries, certificates of origin where relevant, product-safety documentation, and proof of receipt. Screen suppliers, banks, vessels, countries, goods, and end users against applicable EU and French sanctions. Reconcile payment instructions to accounts payable and prohibit split payments or third-party settlement without documented approval.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable forward foreign-exchange contracts for forecast or committed euro and foreign-currency receivables and payables, documented under the bank's master agreement and supported by a genuine commercial exposure.

Non-deliverable forwards for currencies or jurisdictions where physical delivery is restricted or impractical, subject to the counterparty's legal authority, local-market rules, sanctions screening, and the bank's product eligibility requirements. NDFs are generally unnecessary for freely convertible euro exposures.

Currency swaps and cross-currency swaps for managing longer-term shareholder loans, intercompany funding, or recurring currency cash flows, subject to counterparty credit approval, valuation, collateral, and documentation requirements.

Foreign-exchange options, collars, and participating forwards for asymmetric protection of forecast sales, purchases, or committed exposures, subject to suitability, accounting, premium, and transaction-risk review.

Interest-rate and cross-currency derivative documentation should address European Market Infrastructure Regulation obligations, trade reporting, risk-mitigation procedures, clearing or margin requirements where applicable, legal-entity identifiers, and any applicable MiFID corporate-client classification. The SAS should maintain a board-approved treasury policy, exposure forecasts, hedge-designation records, counterparty limits, independent valuation controls, confirmation matching, collateral procedures, and accounting treatment under the applicable reporting framework.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual shareholder approval of accounts and discharge of the president (decision collective annuelle d'approbation des comptes)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal corporate act; signed minutes retained in the corporate decisions register; no filing to a public authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months of fiscal year-end (calendar FY: by 30 June)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-approval triggers civil liability of the president, nullity risk on subsequent acts, and loss of the right to distribute dividends; shareholders may petition the court for a managed inquiry (expertise de gestion).

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of annual accounts, president's report (if required), and resolution with the Commercial Court Registry (depot des comptes annuels)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de commerce (Commercial Court Registry Officer) via the electronic Corporate Formalities Office (guichet unique / infogreffe)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 1 month after shareholder approval; practical final date 31 July for a calendar-year FY (approval on 30 June + 1 month)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing: fine up to EUR 4,500 on the legal representative; court injunction with coercive fine; after repeated default the Registry may initiate administrative strike-off (radiation) and publication of the sanction.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return - annual results declaration (liasse fiscale IS; forms 2065-SD and 2050-2069 schedules)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction generale des Finances publiques (DGFiP) - business tax department (SIE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Second business day after 1 May for calendar-year FY (approx. 5 May 2025); for non-calendar FY, no later than the end of the third month following the closing date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Automatic 10% increase if the tax is unpaid; 40% for intentional omission; 80% for fraudulent concealment; plus late-payment interest of 0.20% per month on the unpaid corporate income tax.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Balance payment and instalment reconciliation of corporate income tax (solde d'impôt sur les sociétés)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DGFiP - SIE tax account via direct debit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due concurrently with the annual return (approx. 5 May for calendar FY); instalments due 15 March, 15 June, 15 September and 15 December
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment: first penalty of 5% plus 0.20% per month interest; compulsory recovery procedures (avis de mise en recouvrement, bank garnishment).

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial ownership register (Registre des beneficiaires effectifs - RBE) accuracy confirmation and dividend-blocking control
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de commerce (RBE register; no separate annual return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Standing update rule: declaration within 30 days of any change in beneficial ownership; verification performed at each annual accounts approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-update: imprisonment up to 6 months and fine up to EUR 7,500 for directors; dividend distributions legally blocked until the register is corrected (art. L.561-47-1 Monetary and Financial Code).

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local business contribution (Cotisation Fonciere des Entreprises - CFE) annual payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction departementale des Finances publiques (DDFiP - local tax office)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Payment due 15 December of the tax year; no annual return for already registered companies; a new taxpayer files form 1447-C-SD by 31 December of the creation year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Automatic 5% increase plus 0.20% monthly interest; missing declaration triggers a EUR 55 flat penalty and possible ex officio assessment.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: CVAE annual return (Cotisation sur la Valeur Ajoutee des Entreprises; form 1330-C) - status for 2025
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Not applicable: CVAE definitively abolished by the 2025 French Finance Act for levies due from 2025 (profits of fiscal years ending on or after 31 December 2024); no return 1330-C, no payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: None - legal obligation cancelled; no residual filing or late-payment exposure for fiscal year 2025.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Final annual DSN social declaration (Declaration Sociale Nominative) and payroll aggregates for the prior year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: URSSAF / Centre national de traitement via the net-entreprises portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Final DSN for December: 5 January for companies with 11+ employees; 15 January for fewer than 11 employees; monthly DSN on the 5th or 15th of the following month
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Flat penalty of EUR 55 per missing declaration (capped at EUR 550); contribution recovery with 5% surcharge and 0.2% monthly late-payment interest.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced rate of 15% on the first EUR 42,000 of taxable profit for eligible SMEs; innovation tax credit (CIR) at 30% on qualifying R&D expenditures up to the statutory cap; patent-box treatment for qualifying industrial property income; young innovative company (JEI) exemption; green industry tax credit for low-carbon investment.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulaire 2065-SD (CERFA n° 11416) together with the liasse fiscale (annexes 2050 to 2059 and 2066); filed electronically through the impots.gouv.fr professional taxpayer portal via EFI or EDI-GFC.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual fiscal return; quarterly equalisation instalments are due on 15 March, 15 June, 15 September and 15 December, with the final balance settled on the annual return.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a fiscal year ended 31 December, the return is due on the second working day following 1 May. For other fiscal years, the return is generally due within three months of the year-end, with special alignment for years closing between 20 September and 31 December.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal form SAS, SIREN, SIRET, NAF/APE code, registered office address, and electronic filing declaration.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The SAS is the French taxpayer. If the entity is a French branch of a foreign company, indicate the French permanent establishment address and the foreign head-office particulars in the accompanying schedules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable result as computed from the accounting result after application of CGI Articles 38 and 209; includes transfer pricing adjustments, depreciation recapture, and reconciliation between book profit and taxable profit via annexes 2058-A and 2058-B.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attribute only effectively connected profits to a French permanent establishment. Payments or expenses routed to non-resident shareholders must be supported by arm's-length evidence and tax residence certificates to be deductible.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Current-year loss and prior-year deficits actually offset against current profit; remaining carryforward triggered under the statutory annual absorption cap.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a French permanent establishment, losses connected with the French business are usable in France. Foreign parent company losses are not reportable to France unless attributed to the same permanent establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box E – Crédits d'Impôt et Réductions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Innovation tax credit, green industry tax credit, foreign tax credit for qualifying foreign-source profits, and other statutory tax credits with supporting computations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders do not enter credits on the SAS return. The SAS may claim foreign tax credit relief only for branch or pass-through income validly attributable to France.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing attracts an automatic 10% increase of assessed tax; the penalty rises to 40% if the return is not corrected within 30 days of a formal notice, and to 80% in cases of bad faith or fraudulent concealment. Monthly moratory interest accrues at 0.20% per month; electronic-filing failures add a fixed EUR 150 penalty and exclusion from certain dispute procedures.
